sense: not to be changed: a final decision

terms.grammar: phrase; with an infinitive, “I have made up my mind to”
evidence: Liv. 2.45.13: certum atque dēcrētum est nōn dare signum
Plaut. Bacch. 382: certumst jam dīcam patrī
Cic. Rosc. Am. 31: certum est dēlīberātumque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The speaker’s last word on a matter: my mind is made up (see decide, and sure).

terms.gloss: settled, fixed, valid, not to be undone
terms.grammar: adjective (participle of reor): ratum esse, ratum habēre
evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.27: dēcrētum stabile, fīxum, ratum esse dēbeat (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ph. 951: quod modo erat ratum, irritum est
terms.comment: Ratum habēre, to treat as final, to confirm; its opposite is irritus, void.

evidence: Cic. Clu. 132: fīxās et in perpetuum ratās (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Post-classical: a surveyors’ and lawyers’ word for boundaries, and “final” only in late philosophy (causa fīnālis). Traupman uses it for the final whistle and the final score.

phrases.latin: itaque certum atque dēcrētum est nōn dare signum, nisi victōrēs sē reditūrōs ex hāc pugnā jūrant
phrases.english: so my decision is final: I will not give the signal unless they swear they will come back from this battle victorious

phrases.latin: Quod dictum, indictum est: quod modo erat ratum, irritum est.
phrases.english: What was said is unsaid; what was settled a moment ago is void.

sources: Lewis & Short: certus · Lewis & Short: decerno · Lewis & Short: ratus · Lewis & Short: reor · Lewis & Short: figo · Lewis & Short: finalis
